- (2) The W2-105 README map lists its parametrised cases with placeholders, such as `test_x[<install>-deny]`, `[<role>-<install>]` and a bare `[pip install requests]`. W2-96's matching code (`src/gov/accept/runner.py:121-131`) reads none of these forms, so their lines report "fail" with zero cases matched, and 22 passing cases are matched to no line.
- (3) The merge queue and the close run the acceptance folder with pytest and do not use `gov accept`'s verdict, so (2) does not block landing.
- (4) No W2-105 case asserts the CTO-only rule. The KPI 2 cases test the kernel's guard rule as it stands, which matches the re-baselined KPI.
risks: Until the map is fixed, anyone who reads only `gov accept`'s top-line outcome sees "fail" for this ticket, although no case failed.
lessons:
- Run the scoped set while the rebuild queues: no selected case read this worktree's store.
- `gov check` takes more than 10 minutes because of gitleaks: start it in the background.
- A README map written before W2-96 needs checking against its matching rules.
proposed_decisions: R-W2-105-1, a residual (it breaks no exit criterion, nothing fails open, and it blocks nothing).
- (a) Recommended, confidence high: a test-designer revision of the README map only, in `tests/acceptance/W2-105/README.md`, rewriting each item as `test_w2_105_install_block.py::<function>`. It carries `Rewrite-Reason: DEC-959 item 6`, changes no test, and rides along with any later resume or W2-90b.
- (b) W2-96's matching code learns the placeholder form: wider, and touches shared code.
- (c) Keep it, and record that `gov accept`'s three "fail" lines for this ticket are a mapping artefact.
